yt_description:
The whole town laughed when Bill sat down to watch a cow pie… until summer. 🪲🐄
Dung beetles roll and bury cow dung, so flies can't breed in it and the soil gets richer. From 1965 to 1985 Australia's CSIRO imported 55 species of dung beetle from Africa, Europe and Hawaii to clean its cattle pastures. (Bill is a fictional character; the beetles are real history.)

Sources: National Museum of Australia, CSIROpedia "Dung beetle program", Wikipedia "Australian Dung Beetle Project".

script: This rancher pays good money for a box of dung beetles. And the whole town thinks he has lost his mind. His pastures are drowning in cow pies. Every cow drops about twelve a day, and they just sit there. The grass dies underneath. And every single cow pie hatches thousands of flies. His neighbor swats, sprays, and drags the field with a heavy chain. Nothing works. But old Bill waits at the train station for a little box that came all the way from Africa. The town laughs. Beetles? You paid money for poop bugs? Then Bill does something even stranger. He puts a chair next to a fresh cow pie, and sits down to watch. The town laughs even louder. He's watching poop! Bill just smiles. And waits. By morning, the cow pie is gone. Rolled into balls, and buried underground. By summer, his grass is thick and green, and the flies are gone. His neighbor's field is one big fly party. That night, the neighbor knocks on his door. Bill... where do I buy poop bugs? Dung beetles really do this. They bury the dung, so flies can't breed in it, and the soil gets richer. Australia imported fifty five species to clean its pastures.
